EcoFlow-Optima: Preliminary Data Analysis

Water Quality, Lake Level and Low-Dissolved-Oxygen Risk in Laguna de Bay

Nepumoceno, F. C.; Nombrado, G. T. G.; Sto Domingo, E. V. A.

November 11, 2026

1 How to rerun this analysis

  1. Keep this file inside the Finals project folder (the one containing 01_cleaned_data, 02_training_candidate, 04_reference_tables).
  2. Open Finals.Rproj in RStudio, then open this file.
  3. Install packages once: install.packages(c("tidyverse", "randomForest", "rmarkdown", "knitr"))
  4. Click Knit (or run chunks one by one with Ctrl+Enter).

Data used: 01_cleaned_data, 02_training_candidate, 04_reference_tables. Not used: 08_unverified_extraction_archive (marked DO NOT TRAIN).

2 Setup and data import

library(tidyverse)
library(randomForest)
set.seed(123)

lake    <- read_csv("01_cleaned_data/lake_numeric_analysis.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
train   <- read_csv("02_training_candidate/train.csv",      show_col_types = FALSE)
valid   <- read_csv("02_training_candidate/validation.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
test    <- read_csv("02_training_candidate/test.csv",       show_col_types = FALSE)
monthly <- read_csv("04_reference_tables/lake_monthly.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
fishkill<- read_csv("04_reference_tables/fish_kill_events.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
floods  <- read_csv("04_reference_tables/bay_flood_history.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
gates   <- read_csv("04_reference_tables/gate_operating_rules.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

Check what parameters exist:

lake %>% count(parameter, unit, sort = TRUE)
lake %>% count(value_status, sort = TRUE)
lake %>% count(numeric_analysis_eligible)

3 Data cleaning and transformation

# Keep rows that are eligible and have a numeric value
lake_clean <- lake
if (any(lake_clean$numeric_analysis_eligible %in% TRUE)) {
  lake_clean <- lake_clean %>% filter(numeric_analysis_eligible %in% TRUE)
}
lake_clean <- lake_clean %>%
  filter(!is.na(numeric_value)) %>%
  mutate(
    date = as.Date(paste0(observation_month, "-01")),
    year = as.integer(format(date, "%Y")),
    month = as.integer(format(date, "%m")),
    param = case_when(
      grepl("oxygen|\\bdo\\b", tolower(parameter)) ~ "DO",
      grepl("bod|biochemical", tolower(parameter)) ~ "BOD",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(param %in% c("DO", "BOD"))

cat("Rows kept:", nrow(lake_clean), "of", nrow(lake), "\n")
## Rows kept: 3384 of 3384
lake_clean %>% count(param, station_id)
# Monthly lake data: parse date
monthly <- monthly %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(paste0(observation_month, "-01")))

# Event tables: extract a start month where it is a clean date
fishkill <- fishkill %>%
  mutate(start_date = suppressWarnings(as.Date(paste0(substr(onset_or_period_start, 1, 7), "-01"))))
floods <- floods %>%
  mutate(start_date = suppressWarnings(as.Date(paste0(substr(event_date_or_period, 1, 7), "-01"))))

# Early-warning screening level (above the 5 mg/L standard) so enough low-DO months exist to evaluate
DO_LIMIT <- 6.5

4 Summary statistics

summ <- function(x) tibble(
  n = sum(!is.na(x)), mean = mean(x, na.rm = TRUE), median = median(x, na.rm = TRUE),
  sd = sd(x, na.rm = TRUE), min = min(x, na.rm = TRUE), max = max(x, na.rm = TRUE))

# Overall by parameter
lake_clean %>% group_by(param) %>% summarise(summ(numeric_value), .groups = "drop")
# By station
station_summary <- lake_clean %>%
  group_by(param, station_id, station_name) %>%
  summarise(summ(numeric_value), .groups = "drop")
station_summary
# Share of DO readings below the screening level, per station
low_do_station <- lake_clean %>%
  filter(param == "DO") %>%
  group_by(station_id, station_name) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mean_DO = mean(numeric_value),
            pct_below_limit = 100 * mean(numeric_value < DO_LIMIT), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(pct_below_limit))
low_do_station
# Readings below the 5 mg/L water-quality standard, per station
lake_clean %>%
  filter(param == "DO") %>%
  group_by(station_id) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), below_5 = sum(numeric_value < 5), pct_below_5 = 100 * mean(numeric_value < 5), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(pct_below_5))
# Lake level and rainfall
monthly %>% summarise(summ(lake_level_mean_m)) %>% mutate(variable = "lake_level_mean_m")
monthly %>% summarise(summ(rainfall_basin_average_mm)) %>% mutate(variable = "rainfall_basin_average_mm")
# Event counts
cat("Fish-kill events on record:", nrow(fishkill), "\n")
## Fish-kill events on record: 9
cat("Flood events on record:", nrow(floods), "\n")
## Flood events on record: 5

5 Visualizations

5.1 Chart 1: Lake level and rainfall with flood events (RQ1)

flood_in_range <- floods %>%
  filter(!is.na(start_date), start_date >= min(monthly$date), start_date <= max(monthly$date))

ggplot(monthly, aes(date, lake_level_mean_m)) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(data = flood_in_range, aes(xintercept = start_date), linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  labs(title = "Mean lake level over time (red dashed = recorded flood event)",
       x = "Month", y = "Lake level (m)") +
  theme_minimal()

ggplot(monthly, aes(date, rainfall_basin_average_mm)) +
  geom_col(fill = "darkgreen") +
  labs(title = "Basin average rainfall by month", x = "Month", y = "Rainfall (mm)") +
  theme_minimal()

5.2 Chart 2: Dissolved oxygen over time by station (RQ2, RQ3)

lake_clean %>%
  filter(param == "DO") %>%
  ggplot(aes(date, numeric_value, color = station_id)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = DO_LIMIT, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  labs(title = paste0("Dissolved oxygen by station (red = ", DO_LIMIT, " mg/L screening level)"),
       x = "Month", y = "DO (mg/L)", color = "Station") +
  theme_minimal()

5.3 Chart 3: Seasonal pattern of DO (RQ3)

lake_clean %>%
  filter(param == "DO") %>%
  ggplot(aes(factor(month), numeric_value)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "lightblue") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = DO_LIMIT, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  labs(title = "DO by calendar month", x = "Month", y = "DO (mg/L)") +
  theme_minimal()

5.4 Chart 4: Stations ranked by share of low-DO readings (RQ2)

ggplot(low_do_station, aes(reorder(station_id, pct_below_limit), pct_below_limit)) +
  geom_col(fill = "orange") + coord_flip() +
  labs(title = paste0("Percent of readings below ", DO_LIMIT, " mg/L by station"),
       x = "Station", y = "% below screening level") +
  theme_minimal()

6 Main statistical analysis

6.1 RQ1: Lake level, rainfall and gate rules

m <- monthly %>% filter(!is.na(lake_level_mean_m), !is.na(rainfall_basin_average_mm)) %>%
  arrange(date) %>%
  mutate(rain_lag1 = lag(rainfall_basin_average_mm), level_change = lake_level_mean_m - lag(lake_level_mean_m))

cor.test(m$lake_level_mean_m, m$rainfall_basin_average_mm)
## 
##  Pearson's product-moment correlation
## 
## data:  m$lake_level_mean_m and m$rainfall_basin_average_mm

6.3 RQ3: Predicting next-month dissolved oxygen (risk of low DO)

Train on train, check on validation, final score on test (time-ordered splits from your files).

feats <- c("do_t_mg_l", "do_t_minus_1_mg_l", "do_t_minus_2_mg_l", "bod_t_mg_l",
           "target_month_sin", "target_month_cos")
target <- "target_do_next_month_mg_l"

prep <- function(d) d %>% select(all_of(c(feats, target))) %>% drop_na()
tr <- prep(train); va <- prep(valid); te <- prep(test)

cat("Train:", nrow(tr), " Validation:", nrow(va), " Test:", nrow(te), "\n")
## Train: 819  Validation: 176  Test: 435
cat("Date ranges (target month):\n")
## Date ranges (target month):
bind_rows(train = range(train$target_month), validation = range(valid$target_month),
          test = range(test$target_month)) %>% print()
## # A tibble: 2 × 3
##   train   validation test   
##   <chr>   <chr>      <chr>  
## 1 2013-04 2023-01    2024-01
## 2 2022-12 2023-12    2026-06
metrics <- function(actual, pred) tibble(
  RMSE = sqrt(mean((actual - pred)^2)), MAE = mean(abs(actual - pred)),
  R2 = 1 - sum((actual - pred)^2) / sum((actual - mean(actual))^2))

# Baseline: next month = this month
base_pred <- te$do_t_mg_l
# Linear regression
lm_fit <- lm(as.formula(paste(target, "~ .")), data = tr)
lm_pred <- predict(lm_fit, te)
# Random forest
rf_fit <- randomForest(as.formula(paste(target, "~ .")), data = tr, ntree = 500)
rf_pred <- predict(rf_fit, te)

# Test set results
results <- bind_rows(
  Baseline_persistence = metrics(te[[target]], base_pred),
  Linear_regression    = metrics(te[[target]], lm_pred),
  Random_forest        = metrics(te[[target]], rf_pred),
  .id = "model")
knitr::kable(results, digits = 3, caption = "Table 1a. Test set (January 2024 to June 2026)")

# Validation set results
val_results <- bind_rows(
  Baseline_persistence = metrics(va[[target]], va$do_t_mg_l),
  Linear_regression    = metrics(va[[target]], predict(lm_fit, va)),
  Random_forest        = metrics(va[[target]], predict(rf_fit, va)),
  .id = "model")

6.3.2 Low-DO warning check

actual_low <- te[[target]] < DO_LIMIT
cat("Low-DO months in test set:", sum(actual_low), "of", length(actual_low), "\n")
## Low-DO months in test set: 69 of 435
warn_eval <- function(pred) {
  pred_low <- pred < DO_LIMIT
  tp <- sum(pred_low & actual_low); fp <- sum(pred_low & !actual_low)
  fn <- sum(!pred_low & actual_low); tn <- sum(!pred_low & !actual_low)
  tibble(TP = tp, FP = fp, FN = fn, TN = tn,
         precision = ifelse(tp + fp > 0, tp / (tp + fp), NA),
         recall = ifelse(tp + fn > 0, tp / (tp + fn), NA))
}
warn_table <- bind_rows(Baseline = warn_eval(base_pred), Linear = warn_eval(lm_pred),
                        Random_forest = warn_eval(rf_pred), .id = "model")
knitr::kable(warn_table, digits = 3,
             caption = "Table 2. Early-warning check at the 6.5 mg/L screening level (test set)")
Table 2. Early-warning check at the 6.5 mg/L screening level (test set)
model TP FP FN TN precision recall
Baseline 23 45 46 321 0.338 0.333
Linear 0 0 69 366 NA 0.000
Random_forest 1 3 68 363 0.250 0.014

  actual_next_month_DO = te[[target]],
  baseline = base_pred,
  linear_regression = lm_pred,

7 Checking calculations

# 1. Recompute one summary by hand
lake_clean %>% filter(param == "DO") %>% summarise(mean = mean(numeric_value), n = n())
# 2. No impossible values
lake_clean %>% group_by(param) %>% summarise(negatives = sum(numeric_value < 0))
# 3. No date leakage: every target month is after its origin month
all(train$target_month > train$origin_month)
## [1] TRUE
# 4. Train dates come before test dates
max(train$target_month) < min(test$target_month)
## [1] TRUE

8 Preliminary interpretation

  • RQ1: Same-month rainfall was weakly and not significantly correlated with lake level (r = 0.25, p = 0.139, n = 36), but the previous month’s rainfall was moderately correlated (r = 0.51, p = 0.002). In a regression on the monthly change in lake level, lagged rainfall was significant (0.00078 m per mm, p = 0.002) while same-month rainfall was not, and the model explained about 33% of the variation (adjusted R² = 0.28). Lake level appears to respond to rainfall with roughly a one-month delay. Both recorded floods (October 2022 and October 2024) fall near the seasonal peak of the lake level. The gate rules are river-stage thresholds, so they could not be tested against lake level.
  • RQ2: Against the 5 mg/L water-quality standard, almost no readings were low (only San Pedro, L_XV, had a few). Using the 6.5 mg/L early-warning screening level, the stations with the highest share of low readings were L_XX (39.1%), L_XIX (18.8%), L_XV (16.4%). DO and BOD had a weak positive correlation (r = 0.26, p < 0.001), which does not fit a simple organic-pollution explanation and may reflect algal productivity, though this cannot be confirmed here. Stations with far fewer readings (L_XX, L_XIX, L_XXI and L_XIII with about 63 to 64 each, and L_XXIV with 18) should be interpreted with care, because small samples and whole-number rounding can inflate the share of readings below the screening level.
  • RQ3: On the test set (435 station-months, January 2024 to June 2026), none of the models predicted next-month DO better than the test average (R² of -0.41 for the baseline, -0.24 for linear regression, -0.33 for random forest). Linear regression had the lowest RMSE (1.07) while the baseline had the lowest MAE (0.76). Current DO and time of year were the only significant predictors. Random forest predictions stayed within a narrow band of about 6.4 to 10.3 mg/L even though actual DO ranged from 4 to 13 mg/L. For the 6.5 mg/L warning, 69 of 435 test months were low. The baseline caught 23 of them (recall 0.33, precision 0.34), linear regression caught none, and random forest caught 1 (recall 0.01). Monthly data alone is therefore not enough for a reliable early-warning model.

9 Limitations

  • Only 9 fish-kill events and 5 flood events are on record, mostly outside the 2013 to 2026 water-quality period, so fish-kill prediction cannot be validated statistically. Low DO is used as a proxy.
  • No stocking density, fish pen count or zone coordinates were available, so crowding (RQ2) is approximated by station water quality.
  • Monthly values hide short low-oxygen episodes that actually cause fish kills.
  • Gate rules are river-stage thresholds, and no gate-operation time series was provided, so gate recommendations cannot be modelled from this data.
  • Correlation does not prove causation.
  • Unverified extractions (08_unverified_extraction_archive) were excluded on purpose.
  • Readings below the 5 mg/L standard were almost absent, so a 6.5 mg/L screening level was used to evaluate the warning model; this is a modelling choice, not a regulatory limit.
  • Recent DO readings appear rounded to whole numbers, so values such as 6 mg/L fall below the screening level and may inflate the flagged months.
  • Rainfall data covers only 36 of 60 months (none for 2020 to 2021).
  • Several stations have far fewer readings than others (L_XXIV has 18; L_XIII, L_XIX, L_XX, L_XXI, L_XXII and L_XXIII have about 63 to 64), so their rankings are less reliable.
